Method 2: The patient’s right arm is extended forward 
perpendicular to the body, with the arm bent so the angle at 
the elbow forms 90 degrees with the fingers pointing up and the 
palm turned away from the body. The greatest breadth across 
the elbow joint is measured with a sliding caliper along the axis 
of the upper arm on the two prominent bones on either side of 
the elbow. This is recorded as the elbow breadth. The following 
tables give the elbow breadth measurements for medium-
framed men and women of various heights (from Metropolitan 
Life Insurance Co., 1983). Measurements lower than those 
listed indicate a small frame size; higher measurements indicate 
a large frame size.
